content:
marie: Heads up — after the CUDA-graph capture change + KV-prefetch turned on, we're seeing comm/compute overlap disappear on 8-GPU tensor-parallel runs. All-reduce shows serialized gaps.
raj: repro link?
emma: timeline pls (nsight or nvprof screenshot)
marie: quick timeline snippet below from Nsight — notice kernels queue up then a long NCCL allreduce window where GPUs idle before/after.
```
GPU0: kernelA -> kernelB -> --- wait NCCL(allreduce) --- -> kernelC
GPU1: kernelA -> kernelB -> --- wait NCCL(allreduce) --- -> kernelC
```
marie: This only happens when we use cudaGraph capture around the KV-cache prefetch + submit batches with stream affinity set to per-GPU compute stream. If I disable capture, overlap returns.
leo: interesting. Could capture be forcing operations onto the default stream during replay? i've seen capture/replay silently enqueue on the graph's stream and break user stream ordering.
jess: do we have a minimal repro? code snip of capture flow?
marie: yes — simplified:
```
// capture on graphStream
cudaStreamBeginCapture(graphStream);
kv_prefetch_async(kv_stream); // pipelined on other stream
launch_forward(graphStream);
cudaStreamEndCapture(graphStream,&graph);
cudaGraphInstantiate(&instance,graph);
cudaGraphLaunch(instance, graphStream);
```
marie: kv_prefetch_async uses async memcpy on a separate stream + recordEvent / waitEvent for compute stream. But on replay the event/wait gets fused differently and seems to serialize before NCCL.
raj: do we see any CUDA error? Also what about CUDA_THREAD_BLOCKING envs? cc @infra-bot for perf traces
infra-bot: attached perf traces: /artifacts/1869001234/nvtx_trace.json (uploaded)
emma: looking at the trace: the event wait for kv prefetch is replayed as a host synchronization in capture path (there's a call to cudaStreamWaitEvent that ends up serialized on the graph stream during replay). That would explain the gap before NCCL.
leo: NCCL/allreduce needs to overlap with compute on separate streams — if capture forces the compute stream to wait, overlap lost.
jess: could be kernel selection changes too — maybe replay picks different kernel variant with larger shared mem causing longer launch? check kernel names in trace.
marie: kernel names look same, but launch durations increase ~10-15%. And allreduce wall time increases because scheduling gap causes more serialized traffic.
raj: hypothesis: capture changes stream semantics -> cudaGraphReplay serializes event waits -> our batching heuristic that hoped to prefetch KV on 'transfer' stream gets demoted. Repro steps: run 8 GPU TP, enable KV-prefetch, enable cuda-graphs capture on per-batch path. Observe throughput drop ~20%.
emma: quick test: if you move kv_prefetch to the default stream (so capture includes it) does overlap return?
marie: tried that — overlap partially restored but we lose batching benefits. Prefetching on transfer stream is desired.
leo: possible fixes: 1) use graphNode with memcpys integrated into graph so no inter-stream events, 2) replace event/wait with semaphores that are preserved across capture/replay? Not sure.
jess: also consider NCCL async progress mode / enablecudaGraph support in NCCL? maybe NCCL needs to be capture-aware.
raj: I'll try a patch: during graph capture, record memcpys as graph nodes or temporarily disable the event wait pattern (use streamPeer copies into the capture stream). Will run perf tonight.
marie: thanks. If anyone can repro locally, try comparing nvtx traces with/without capture and post the short nvprof snippets. Also add kernel selection flags to rule out different launch choices (set FORCE_KERNEL_VARIANT=...)
emma: logged as eng-runtime ticket #IR-3721 with trace links.
jess: cc @platform-team in case scheduling changes needed.
leo: one last thought — batching heuristics might increase seq length variance which changes kernel selection thresholds; combine that with capture timing could amplify the stall. keep an eye on seqLen distribution in that run.
marie: good point. attaching small CSV of seqLen hist: /artifacts/1869001234/seq_hist.csv
raj: ok will update tomorrow with perf numbers. :coffee:
emma: thx all :thumbsup:
